desc: The uplifting, fun and danceable sounds of COLOMBIA shine throughout this release from multi-instrumentalist composer and vocalist Danny Osuna. These CUMBIAS and VALLENATOS feature playful accordion work along with lively lyrics and percussion.

tracks.desc: "Tell me what you like" and "Tell me what you wish for" are the catch-phrases of this happy and warm CUMBIA about cooking, cuisine and good food. All the musical seasonings of this cheery song are in place -- the sticky unison riff played by the accordion and guitar, plus the bubbling keys and guitars accompanied by the hand percussion, timbale drums and wood blocks. Great for cooking shows, restaurant features and travel reviews.

This joyous VALLENATO is about the emotive power of good music, especially how it brings forth a sense of goodness, release and escape form the day to day struggles. "Vallenato" literally means "born in the valley", as the genre mostly comes from the Caribbean region of Colombia. Colombia's traditional vallenato music is a fundamental part of their cultural heritage. The track features some very hip bass double-stops in the intro and catchy accordion work.

This perky, uptempo CUMBIA about a love crush and longing for a lost connection features the maiden vocals of RAIN BISOU (Rina Guadalupe Cervantes), an accomplished and classically trained Latin-American singer currently based in Los Angeles. This catchy, dance-able track features Rain's slick vocal harmonies and Danny's lively accordion work that really shines during the breakdowns (when the timbale drums lay out).

Contrast, double-meanings and hand percussion are driving forces of this mid-tempo VALLENATO about a surprise party. Behind the cheerful music lies a hidden warning of a celebration meant to lure enemies that are due what's coming to them. No problem for the general public, but if you are in the game, watch your back, as justice will not wait. "Let the music make you dance, let whoever wants to sing, sing, but tonight you will face unavoidable revenge".

"Dangerous Serpentine". This CUMBIA delivers a straight-up villainess theme about a treacherous woman to be avoided at all costs, a lady viper with poison in her veins. Great track for Halloween and Horror films / shows. Cool features of this song are the call and response chorus and the groovy marimba playing in unison with the accordion, giving it a nice regional texture and differentiating flavor.

Featuring the maiden vocals of Rain Bisou, this vivacious VALLENATO delivers a message of playful seduction, but be careful, she may be your future "Black Window". "Vallenato" literally means "born in the valley", as the genre mostly comes from the Caribbean region of Colombia. Colombia's traditional vallenato music is a fundamental part of their cultural heritage. The track features fun, flirty lyrics plus Danny's very hip accordion and acoustic guitar work.
